items.title: Vercel Sandbox snapshot creation is now up to 10x faster
items.text: now creates snapshots up to 10x faster. Median time to snapshot is under 0.4 seconds, down from 4.4 seconds. Snapshot restore speed has also improved by 50% from 500ms to 250ms at p50.Vercel Sandbox Snapshots are now able to write and restore by re-using frames within the Vercel Hive Snapshot (VHS) format. VHS now indexes data in a more efficient way which means that more read and write operations can be done in parallel. Snapshots can now restore more of your Sandbox base image in parallel with user data, leading to overall faster operations. Persistent sandboxes, the default, snapshot automatically when a session stops and resume from the latest snapshot. This applies to all new snapshots, with nothing to configure. Existing snapshots keep the previous format. Learn more in the .snapshots documentation Read more

items.title: Decision models take 26% of requests; Anthropic now wins new teams 2:1
items.text: AI Gateway Production Index — November 2026 Every month, routes more than 100 trillion tokens between production applications and AI labs. That traffic gives us a view of what AI usage looks like in today’s enterprise and startup landscape across language, decision, voice, image, and video models. We publish it here monthly. See the Production Index reports from , , and .AI GatewayAugustSeptemberOctober Production AI is splitting into two jobs: generation and judgment. Until recently, when software needed to make a quick call, a team could use either a fixed rule that was cheap but rigid, or a language model that was smart but slow and expensive. Decision models are now a third option. They classify, score, or pick between choices instead of generating text, and cost about a seventieth as much per request as a language model. They arrived on AI Gateway in mid-September, and there are now 15 decision models available from eight different vendors. In October, nearly a third of paid teams on AI Gateway used a decision model. items.title: Workflow SDK now writes over WebSockets on Vercel
items.text: The now sends event writes and stream writes to over a WebSocket by default, replacing one HTTP request per write, or per write group for streams. No code change is needed beyond upgrading to or later.Workflow SDKVercel Workflowsworkflow@5.2.0 Once you deploy the upgrade, new runs use it. In-flight runs finish on the deployment they started on. Existing streaming code works as is. A step that writes a burst of chunks, like AI tokens, sends them over the WebSocket once it opens: In a replaying an AI agent's token stream, v5.2.0, which writes streams over a WebSocket by default, delivered the full response 4.2× faster than v4.8.12, with no chunk delayed over a second.benchmark Every step start and completion is an event write, now sent over the WebSocket, so workflows with many steps make fewer HTTP requests. The added efficiency also improves performance and reduces costs. The queue handler opens the connection for every delivery. Read the to get started. If you're on 4.x, start with the , since v5 is a major release.Vercel World documentationupgrade guide Read more Streams keep pace with AI output Fewer HTTP requests for event writes Get started

items.title: Build disk space on Vercel increased to 64 GB
items.text: Disk space for has increased from 32 GB to 64 GB on Basic and Standard machines, matching the capacity already available on Enhanced and Turbo.Vercel builds The additional space provides more room for the packages your project uses and the files generated during a build, reducing the risk of running out of disk space. The change applies automatically across all plans and build machine types at no additional charge, with no configuration changes required. Learn more in the .build machine documentation Read more

items.title: Malicious bee-js npm Release and Swarm Desktop Releases Deliver SleepyDuck Ethereum C2 Backdoor
items.text: Socket’s Threat Research Team analyzed the November 9, 2026 compromise of Ethersphere’s release pipeline, in which a threat actor used the project’s own GitHub automation to publish a malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 to npm and a trojanized Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 release on GitHub. Both artifacts carry a small loader that fetches JavaScript from api[.]frameworkmetrics[.]xyz and executes it with full Node.js privileges. The Ethereum smart contract that tells the later stages where to connect, the wallet that controls it, and the stage-3 implant files are the same ones Pluto Security documented on October 1, 2026 in its analysis of the SleepyDuck / EtherDuck Open VSX campaign. npm removed 13.3.0 about 75 minutes after it was published; the Swarm Desktop release stayed up for about eight and a half hours. @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 (npm): scripts/generate-version.cjs was rewritten into a remote-code loader and promoted to a postinstall hook. The package was published by Ethersphere’s legitimate trusted-publishing workflow with valid SLSA provenance, and the loader ran three times inside that publishing job.
